clue.text: An Identikit label?

parts.note: Identikit suggests a police picture of a suspect, but read it as 'identify kit': a sewn-in strip naming the owner of school clothes

explanation.surface: A question about the caption on a police composite portrait of a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Identikit is a police system for building a suspect's face; here it splits into ID-ENTI-KIT, the job of a strip of fabric sewn into a child's school uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a woven strip, stitched into clothing, carries the owner's printed name so lost garments can be returned.

clue.text: Hunter's puzzling variation of theme

definitions.meaning: the mighty hunter of Genesis is named in the Bible
Elgar's Enigma Variations contains a famous movement with this title

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible calls him a mighty hunter, and Elgar named the best-known of his Enigma Variations after him.

clue.text: Tempest, for example, enveloping N Sea painting

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the actress's name goes around the letter

parts.note: Dame Marie Tempest was a famous English actress
N is taken as printed

explanation.surface: A storm wraps a picture of the North Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'N Sea' looks like the North Sea, but N is a lone letter and 'Sea painting' is the definition; Marie Tempest was a star of the Edwardian stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape picture, a work of art depicting ships or ocean, is a genre of that name.

clue.text: Book attendant at start of work

parts.note: a book is a title in publishing
a page is a young attendant to a knight or noble

explanation.surface: A book's servant arrives as the job begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book giving its name and author begins the work.

clue.text: Group have right to new printing process

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are formed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A band are entitled to a novel way of printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GROUP, HAVE, R and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an engraving method transferring photographs to copper plates for print reproduction.

clue.text: Like the number at the beginning or end of a race

definitions.text: Like the number at the beginning or end of a race

parts.words: Like the number at the beginning or end of a race
parts.note: the numerals painted on runners' bibs and posted at finishing lines are of the Western kind that came to Europe from the Middle East, and the word also names a people

explanation.surface: A remark about the numeral seen at a race's start or finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The race in the surface is an athletics race, but the word also hints at a race in the ethnic sense, the people whose numeral system we use.
explanation.definitionFit: Our ordinary digits 1 to 9 are known as the numerals of the Arabs, so race numbers are in that script.

clue.text: She is Belgian, according to Meredith's 3

definitions.text: She is Belgian, according to Meredith's 3

parts.words: She is Belgian, according to Meredith's 3
parts.note: one of George Meredith's novels names its heroine on the title page with a surname meaning a person from Flanders

explanation.surface: A woman's nationality as stated on the front leaf of a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to 3 down: the title page of Meredith's novel 'Rhoda Fleming' shows her surname, and a Fleming is a native of Flanders in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine's surname in George Meredith's novel means a Flemish person, so she counts as from Belgium.

clue.text: -Palatial old aeroplane

definitions.meaning: suggests the great Oxfordshire palace given to the Duke of Marlborough
the Bristol bomber of the Second World War bore this name

explanation.walkthrough: The dash before the clue is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxfordshire stately home of the Marlboroughs is a palace, and Bristol built a 1930s bomber of that name.

clue.text: Join a shy motion picture artist on the line

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: cine is short for cinematograph, motion picture film
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A bashful film painter boards a train.
explanation.walkthrough: Join 'a shy' and you get ASHY, the definition; RA (Royal Academician) and RY (railway) are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to ashes, as of a cremation urn, which is to say powdery and grey.

clue.text: Revolutionary peer's son on his feet a long time in this

definitions.text: on his feet a long time in this

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
Hon (Honourable) is the courtesy title given to a peer's son

explanation.surface: A radical aristocrat's boy stands for hours at some event.
explanation.walkthrough: HON, short for Honourable, is the style a British peer's younger son carries before his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance footrace keeps each runner going on foot for hours, matching the event someone stays upright through.

clue.text: Gloomy resort, Lemnos

indicators.note: to re-sort the letters is to arrange them again in a new order

explanation.surface: Lemnos, the Greek island, is a dreary holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place describing the Greek island of Lemnos, but read it as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a serious, sombre mood without cheer.

clue.text: Namby-pamby makes the fairway twice

indicators.note: twice means the word is given two times

parts.note: in old golf slang the mown fairway was known as the pretty

explanation.surface: A soppy person improves the golf course two times over.
explanation.walkthrough: Golfers once called the fairway 'the pretty'; 'makes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something affectedly dainty or insipidly sweet, over-refined.

clue.text: Predator recognized in Troy

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of Central Asia goes by this name, a hunting big cat
troy weight, used for precious metals, has this unit as one of its recognised measures

explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is an Asian hunting cat, and in troy weight a unit of 480 grains is one of the standard measures.

clue.text: Prayer adapted to the ear of Ruth

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Words of devotion rewritten to suit Ruth's hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges the nine letters of EAR OF RUTH; 'to the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer, taught by Jesus, is known by its two opening words.

clue.text: Dog finds soldier on heap of stones

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the soldier comes after the stones

parts.note: a cairn is a pile of stones raised as a landmark or memorial
a terrier is old slang for a member of the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: A dog discovers a soldier perched on a pile of rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' uses British slang for a volunteer in the Territorial Army, the part-time reserve; in an across clue 'on' places that piece after the heap of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, shaggy Scottish breed bred to hunt among rocky piles, one type of hound.

clue.text: The — minds of innkeepers" (Chesterton)

parts.note: a missing word from Chesterton's poem praising landlords who treat men to a bottle

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-gap quotation from a G K Chesterton poem about publicans.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Chesterton's 'The Song Against Grocers': 'The righteous minds of innkeepers / Induce them now and then / To crack a bottle with a friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton praises publicans as upright and virtuous, morally just, in his song.

clue.text: Shut up about a Test opener being too young

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the walling-in word goes round the rest

parts.note: to immure is to wall in or imprison

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Confined for being too young to open the batting in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test opener' looks like a cricket batsman, but it is just the first letter T; 'about' puts IMMURE around A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being not yet grown or developed means one is not old enough.

clue.text: Change duties in part

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alter the share of tasks you do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges DUTIES IN; 'part' is a verb, to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To part people or things is to split or sever them.

clue.text: First trip takes girl messenger a long time

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl or young woman
an envoy is a messenger sent on a mission
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An inaugural journey sees a young woman courier delay for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's first ever voyage, its inaugural trip, is named this.

clue.text: Dissolve, an international bond

parts.note: un is French for 'a' or 'an', a foreign article
a knot is a tie or bond

explanation.surface: Break up a global treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: UN is the French for 'an', hence 'an international'.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie or undo something, such as a tangle, is to loosen or break it up.

clue.text: They posed for a long time as gods in human form

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed is sat
YRS is short for years, a long time

explanation.surface: Models sitting for ages to represent deities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' and 'for' only link; the woodland creatures of myth are half-human gods.
explanation.definitionFit: These woodland spirits of Greek myth were deities shaped as men with goatish features.

clue.text: Mature but very hesitant breaker of the marriage bed

parts.note: mature means grown up, fully adult

indicators.note: very intensifies, so the hesitation noise is doubled

parts.note: er is the sound of a hesitating speaker

explanation.surface: A grown-up but nervous man cheats on his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very hesitant' doubles the hesitation noise ER; 'but' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits infidelity violates the vows of wedlock, the old phrase being to defile the nuptial bed.

clue.text: Prepare for strike

parts.note: it looks like workers getting ready for industrial action, but it is a golfer placing the ball before hitting it

explanation.surface: A union gets ready for industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: The strike is not a walkout but a golf shot: you set the ball on a peg first.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer sets the ball on a peg before driving, readying the shot.

clue.text: The islanders are naturally friendly here

definitions.text: The islanders are naturally friendly here

parts.words: The islanders are naturally friendly here
parts.note: Captain Cook called this Pacific group the Friendly Islands, so friendliness is its name

explanation.surface: A traveller's comment on the warm welcome of some island people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pacific kingdom was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook in 1773.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polynesian kingdom's nickname, given by Cook, is the Friendly Islands.

clue.text: Joined football team

definitions.meaning: joined means linked or brought together
many football clubs carry this word, Manchester and Leeds among them

explanation.definitionFit: Joined means combined into one, and several British football clubs, such as Manchester and Newcastle, bear this name.

clue.text: Sir Joseph Porter was office boy to one

definitions.text: Sir Joseph Porter was office boy to one

parts.words: Sir Joseph Porter was office boy to one
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore Sir Joseph sings that as a lad he served a lawyer's firm

explanation.surface: A biographical note about the comic First Lord of the Admiralty's early job.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Joseph Porter is the First Lord of the Admiralty in HMS Pinafore, whose song 'When I was a lad' tells how he 'served a term as office boy' to this kind of lawyer's firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer who employed the boy was a legal practitioner acting for clients, as the song says.

clue.text: On late? A new temp is not liable

parts.note: late means former, which is ex

indicators.note: new signals the word temp is made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Arriving late, a fresh temporary worker escapes blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles the word temp, which then follows the word for former; 'On' and 'A' only link, and 'late' means former, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being freed from a duty or obligation means not being answerable for it.

clue.text: Scorpion-grass — a name to remember

definitions.meaning: scorpion-grass is an old country name for the forget-me-not plant
the plant's common name, forget-me-not, is a plea to be remembered

explanation.definitionFit: This botanical genus is the forget-me-not, also called scorpion-grass, whose common name asks to be recalled.
